title: Feet Like a Deer’s
old_p1: Habakkuk was a prophet long ago, a man who speaks for Heavenly Father. Hard times were coming to his land.
Habakkuk sang a prayer. He said that even if the fig trees did not bloom, and no grapes grew, and the sheep were gone…
“Yet I will rejoice in the Lord,” Habakkuk said. Rejoice means to be very glad. Even in hard times, he would be glad in the Lord.
old_p2: He sang, “The Lord is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet.” A hind is a deer. Deer climb steep, rocky hills and do not fall. The Lord would help Habakkuk walk strong in hard, high places.
When something feels hard, the Lord can make you strong. Tonight, wiggle your feet, then let them rest. He will help you climb.
p1: Habakkuk looked ahead and knew hard days might come. What if the fig trees had no fruit? What if no grapes grew? What if the sheep were gone and the fields were empty?
Even then, Habakkuk made a brave choice. He would rejoice in the Lord. His joy did not have to disappear when life was difficult, because the Lord would still be his strength.
p2: Habakkuk sang about a deer climbing a steep, rocky hill. Watch how its strong feet find a place to stand, one careful step at a time. Habakkuk trusted that the Lord would help him stand strong in hard places too.

Some things are difficult, even for brave people. You can ask Heavenly Father for strength and keep trying. Tonight, wiggle your toes like a deer finding its footing. The Lord can help you take the next step.
note: Levi, 20 Nov 2026 ("Match up the story lantern stories with the published book"): p1 and p2 are the story words AS PRINTED in the published December book (We Have Waited for Him, on Amazon), first and second story page, word for word, so the Lantern, the app's Books page and the book a family bought read the same. The Christian edition reads God for Heavenly Father; p2_christian only where the printed words are Latter-day Saint teaching. The 29 Oct picture-book rewrite is kept as rewrite_p1/rewrite_p2.
rewrite_p1: Habakkuk told the people what Heavenly Father said. He knew hard times were coming to his land.
So Habakkuk sang a prayer. Maybe the fig trees would not bloom. Maybe no grapes would grow, and the sheep would be gone.
“Yet I will rejoice in the Lord,” Habakkuk sang. Even with empty fields, he would still be glad in the Lord.
rewrite_p2: He sang, “The Lord is my strength.” He said the Lord would make his feet like a deer’s feet. Deer climb steep, rocky hills and do not slip. The Lord would help Habakkuk walk strong in hard, high places.
When something feels hard, the Lord can make you strong too. Tonight, wiggle your feet, then let them rest. He will help you climb.
